o1.biggest_strength: Takes the 4.0 apart line by line against the 2.5 break-even, shows non-brand Google lost about $20,000, and proves it with a segment table that adds exactly to $144,960.
o1.biggest_mistake: No concrete ad copy or feed attribute work (size, colour, material, highlights), so the customer's words only appear in one title line rather than in headlines and feed fields.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add ready-to-paste search headlines and descriptions in Claire's and Nina's own words, plus the missing feed fields (size, colour, material, highlights), without losing the per-line profit ranges.

o2.biggest_strength: Sharp, on-brand execution: customer-language headlines and a gentle target-ROAS ramp (2.6 then 3.0) so PMax does not stall after the brand exclusion.
o2.biggest_mistake: The base case leans on brand search turning $18,000 into $455,000 (ROAS ~25) versus $204,000 from $12,000 last month, and the cautious case never stress-tests that single assumption that carries 40% of projected value.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Show brand-search value as a defensible range instead of a 95%-retention leap, and pull bags out of PMax so the scaled bags campaign is not bidding against itself.

reason: Output 1 is the one I could take to the CFO: every number traces to my data, the profit ranges are conservative and per line, the feed gap and the bags-inside-PMax cannibalisation are both caught, and it tells me to judge the month on total profit and new customers rather than PMax's own ROAS. Output 2 has better ad copy and a smarter ROAS ramp, but its brand-search assumption is a leap I would have to unpick before trusting the base case.
